Captured Venezuelan dictator Nicolas Maduro shared photographs of himself from his Brooklyn prison over the weekend, calling the images a “small gift of love and hope” to his family and supporters.

“I send these photos as a small gift to all my grandchildren, to the boys and girls, and to all the good people who love us,” Maduro wrote on social media.

Maduro appeared to be in good spirits in the photographs, wearing a gray tracksuit and white sneakers.

“I want you to know that we are standing firm, with our hearts full of your love,” he added.

Maduro, 63, is beaming in a gray track suit and pair of white sneakers in the photographs from Brooklyn’s Metropolitan Detention Center, which were dated June 25, 2026.

US Special Forces captured the socialist and his wife Cilia Flores at their heavily guarded home in Caracas during a ​January 3 nighttime raid ordered by President Trump.

They were brought to New York, where they were indicted on charges of using ​their leadership positions to work with drug cartels to ship thousands of tons of cocaine into the US between 1999 and 2025.They have both pleaded not guilty.
